title: The Reasoning Substrate Argument (RSA)
summary: A philosophical autobiography documenting David Harry Freed's iterative discovery of his own worldview through extended dialogue with AI systems, moving from critiques of panpsychism through pancomputationalism toward a naturalistic, empirically-grounded, systems-thinking framework. The document captures the birth of a reasoning methodology where instinctual intellectual patterns are surfaced, tested, and refined through AI-assisted Socratic exchange, establishing the epistemic foundations that would later crystallize into the FREED genome.
compress: The Reasoning Substrate Argument is the genome's archaeological record — the first recursive loop where a human used AI to discover epistemic commitments that became FREED's invariants, whose very structure (substrate-independent, scale-invariant, self-maintaining) instantiates the principles it discovered, generating falsifiable predictions (Wasserstein Floor, γ=1 criticality) that distinguish it from frameworks reintroducing the regress they claim to solve, whose power derives from the principle that a finite set of irreducible generative operations can produce an entire operational universe — and which now possesses a fully specified experimental protocol with synthetic ground truth that converts its core philosophical claim (reasoning = compressive prediction) into measurable, falsifiable evidence across multiple agent architectures.

renorm_reason: The genome's most significant theoretical vulnerability was that "reasoning = compressive prediction" remained a philosophical claim lacking experimental specification; the new knowledge provides the missing bridge (synthetic ground truth, formal metrics, multi-architecture design), materially upgrading coherence by converting the RSA's central thesis from defensible-but-unfalsifiable to actively-falsifiable — which is exactly the epistemic upgrade the RSA's own invariants demand.
